The first thing validation catches is the `await params` at the top level. 217 218 ### Step 2: Fix the validation error 219 220 There is no `generateStaticParams` here, `slug` is only known at request time. Because awaiting `params` suspends, the page component can't do it at the top level. Instead, move the `await params` into separate components, pass `params` to each, and wrap them with ``. 221 222 For each component, decide: 223 224 **Product details** (name, price) rarely change. Cache the data function with `use cache`: 225 226 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 227 async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 228 const { slug } = await params 229 const product = await getProduct(slug) 230 return ( 231 <> 232

{product.name}

234 235 ) 236 } 237 238 async function getProduct(slug: string) { 239 'use cache' 240 return db.products.findBySlug(slug) 241 } 242 ``` 243 244 > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 245 246 **Inventory** must be fresh each request. Leave it uncached: 247 248 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 249 async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 250 const { slug } = await params 251 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 252 return

281 How validation simulates different navigations 282 283 When you add `unstable_instant` to a route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 284 285 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 286 287 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 288 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 289 290 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 291 292
293 294 ## Opting out with `instant = false` 295 296 Not every layout or page can be instant. A dashboard layout that reads cookies and fetches user-specific data might be too dynamic for the first visit. You can set `instant = false` on any layout or page to exempt it from validation: 297 298 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 299 export const unstable_instant = false 300 ``` 301 302 This tells validation: navigating to `/dashboard` from outside does not need to be instant, but sibling navigations within it still do. Navigating from `/dashboard/a` to `/dashboard/b` can still be checked by adding `instant` to the page segments under `/dashboard`. 303 304 ## Next steps 305 306 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for all configuration options, including runtime prefetching and incremental adoption with `instant = false` 307 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 308 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 309

events.content:
Fixed. Navigating from home to the product page now shows the title immediately; only the inventory streams in afterward. The problem: in `app/product/page.tsx`, the page component itself awaited `getInventory()`, which is uncached dynamic data (`lib/data.ts` calls `connection()`). With Cache Components enabled, uncached data outside a `` boundary makes a client navigation **blocking** — the home page stays visible until the server finishes rendering, so nothing (including the title) appears until the fetch completes. The fix, following this version's `instant-navigation` guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`: - Moved the `getInventory()` call into a child `Inventory` component wrapped in `Checking availability...

}>`, so the `

Premium Widget

` is part of the static shell that renders instantly on navigation while stock and price stream in. - Added `export const unstable_instant = true`, which makes Next.js validate during development that navigating to this route stays instant — if someone later adds blocking data access, the dev overlay flags it. Verified with `npm run build`: `/product` now reports as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content — instead of a fully dynamic route.
